expected_evidence: geological: an anomalous sediment layer at ~12,900 cal BP (the Younger Dryas boundary 'black mat') across North American sites, showing either a distinct volcanic tephra/ash horizon with matching geochemical signature, OR extraterrestrial impact/airburst proxies (platinum and iridium anomalies, magnetic and glassy microspherules, nanodiamonds) — note these are two different, largely incompatible signatures depending on whether the actor is truly volcanic or truly cosmic

astronomical/geological: a corresponding sulfate or ash spike in Greenland and Antarctic ice cores dated to ~10,950 BCE, distinguishing volcanic sulfate aerosol loading from cosmic-impact dust/soot signatures
material: a continent-wide charcoal/biomass-burning spike and disruption or abandonment horizon at Clovis-era archaeological sites coincident with the cooling onset
genetic: a North American megafaunal extinction/population-bottleneck signature and a human population genetic bottleneck dated to the YD onset

model_prior: existing paleoclimate/archaeological literature on the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (Firestone et al. and successors) and on YD volcanic-forcing hypotheses, plus critiques disputing reproducibility of the proposed markers
response.rationale: The Younger Dryas onset (~10,950 BCE) is one of the most intensively studied paleoclimate boundaries, with well-preserved ice-core, lake-sediment, and archaeological records across North America, so relevant geological (0.65) and astronomical/ice-core (0.7) proxies are highly likely to have survived and been searched for — and indeed the real-world Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis debate shows this evidence class has been actively pursued and contested. Material (0.35) and genetic (0.3) traces are less directly diagnostic of a specific trigger mechanism and more prone to preservation gaps and multiple confounding causes (overkill, climate stress), so absence there is less informative. A notable issue with this specific hypothesis is internal incoherence: it names a 'volcanic-eruption' actor but a 'cosmic-airburst' mechanism, which are distinct and largely non-overlapping causal pathways in the literature (volcanic sulfate forcing vs. extraterrestrial impact/airburst proxies) — this looks like a hybridized or mis-specified hypothesis rather than a coherent single claim, which should temper confidence in any evidence gathered under it. Given the generally good preservation and active scientific scrutiny of this exact period/event, low detectability is not a strong excuse for absence of confirming impact-specific markers, though the volcanic-vs-cosmic ambiguity itself lowers how cleanly any found evidence could be attributed. This assessment relies partly on model-prior knowledge of the YDIH debate, which should be treated as unverified background rather than an established fact for this specific hypothesis instance.
